# Draft:David T. Warner draft while we await undeletion of the existing draft that was previously deleted and which recreation has been denied

His 1998 novel about sheriff Jim Turner was reissued in 2004 with a new cover and more illustrations. The Gainesville Sun reported the book "The book is the story of Warner's distant cousin, James Turner, who was elected sheriff of Levy County five times by the time he was 80 years old" and is told "through Sheriff Turner's vantage point - his front porch in Fowler's Bluff, overlooking the Suwanee River" and "is the story of 1900 rural Florida." The Sub reported his book on Bimini Island, "introduces readers to the eclectic personalities of the people of the island - the fishermen and smugglers, the Hemingway scholars and the Hemingway compatriots, the lawless and the lovelorn - and recounts the adventures they lived."
Warner was a contributing editor for Gulfshore Life and Sarasota Magazine. He lived in Lochloosa, Florida near Cross Creek.
UFO film screened at Bellamy Road in 2006 with questions and answers.
